hints: Focus on what complete combustion means for compounds containing C, H and O, and what products must form.
Write the balanced equation for ethanol, C2H5OH, first and count how many O2 it really needs.
Now balance ethyne and ethanal the same way and see which two both need exactly 2.5 mol of O2 per mole.
walkthrough:
**Recall complete combustion**

Complete combustion of C, H, O compounds always gives carbon dioxide and water only.

$$\text{C}_x\text{H}_y\text{O}_z + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow x\text{CO}_2 + \frac{y}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Balance C, then H, then O to find moles of $\text{O}_2$.

**Test compound 1, ethanol**

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}$.

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O} + 3\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Check O atoms: left has 1 + 6 = 7, right has 4 + 3 = 7. So 1 mol needs 3 mol $\text{O}_2$, not 2.5. Statement 1 is out.

**Test compound 2, ethyne**

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ has no oxygen to help.

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_2 + 2.5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Check O atoms: left has 5, right has 4 + 1 = 5. So 1 mol needs exactly 2.5 mol $\text{O}_2$. Statement 2 fits.

**Test compound 3, ethanal**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$.

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O} + 2.5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Check O atoms: left has 1 + 5 = 6, right has 4 + 2 = 6. So 1 mol also needs exactly 2.5 mol $\text{O}_2$. Statement 3 fits.

Therefore only 2 and 3 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Compound 1 needs 3 mol O2, not 2.5 mol, so it cannot be included.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims 1 and 2 only. It wrongly includes ethanol which needs 3 mol O2, and wrongly excludes ethanal which does need 2.5 mol O2.
options.C: Correct. Only 2 and 3 need 2.5 mol O2. Ethyne gives 2CO2 + H2O and ethanal gives 2CO2 + 2H2O, both balanced with 2.5 O2, while ethanol needs 3 O2.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims 1 only. Ethanol needs 3 mol O2 per mole for complete combustion to 2CO2 + 3H2O, so it does not match the 2.5 mol requirement.
